# google-deepmind/alphafold3 (commit c0f97eda2f1f482fd94d3a38bece18c7069b4a5c)
# google-deepmind/alphafold3 Overview
The AlphaFold 3 repository predicts the 3D structures of biological molecules and their complexes. It transforms diverse biological input data into structured features and employs a neural network to generate atomic coordinates and confidence metrics.

The system provides Docker images for configuring the development and runtime environment. These images ensure consistent dependency management, HMMER installation, and GPU optimization. Specialized scripts manage Solid State Drives for large biological databases, particularly in cloud environments. See [Setup and Environment Configuration](#setup-and-environment-configuration) for more information.

It parses and preprocesses various biological data formats, including CIF, FASTA, and Multiple Sequence Alignments. High-performance C++ implementations with Python bindings handle data extraction and serialization efficiently. This enables the conversion of raw biological data into a structured format. [Data Parsing and Preprocessing](#data-parsing-and-preprocessing) covers these processes.

The repository generates input features for the model from parsed biological data. This includes creating Multiple Sequence Alignments, identifying structural templates, and preparing molecular information using external tools like HMMER and RDKit. The featurization pipeline orchestrates these processes, often in parallel. More details are in [Input Feature Generation](#input-feature-generation).

Molecular structures are represented using an immutable, array-based data model. This robust system aggregates chains, residues, atoms, and bonds, facilitating structural analysis and manipulation. It specifically handles biological assemblies and chemical component data. [Molecular Structure Management](#molecular-structure-management) describes these internal representations.

The core model architecture processes input features through several neural network components:
*   An Evoformer/Pairformer refines single and pair representations.
*   Atom-level cross-attention mechanisms integrate atomic information.
*   A generative diffusion denoising process predicts atom positions.
These components are implemented using Haiku modules and JAX for efficient computation. Further details are in [Core Model Architecture and Pipeline](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline).

JAX-compatible geometric primitives handle 3D vectors, rotation matrices, and rigid transformations. These primitives utilize a struct-of-arrays design, enabling efficient batch operations and seamless integration with JAX's capabilities. It supports calculations for distances, angles, and weighted means. See [Geometric Primitives and Operations](#geometric-primitives-and-operations) for more information.

The system includes functionalities for scoring and evaluating predicted molecular structures. This involves structural alignment, RMSD calculations, and chirality detection and comparison for ligands. It also generates pseudo-beta atom positions for quality assessment. [Model Scoring and Evaluation](#model-scoring-and-evaluation) provides more details.

A set of foundational utilities and constants support the codebase. This includes configuration management, secure data loading through restricted pickling, and access to atom types, chemical component definitions, and periodic table data. These ensure consistent data handling and reliable operations. [Common Utilities and Constants](#common-utilities-and-constants) describes these shared resources.

## Setup and Environment Configuration
The AlphaFold 3 environment setup is primarily managed through Docker, which orchestrates the installation of system dependencies, Python packages, HMMER, and crucial configurations for XLA optimization on GPUs. This ensures a consistent and reproducible development and runtime environment. Complementary scripts are provided for efficient management of Solid State Drives (SSDs), particularly for handling large public databases within cloud environments.

The core of the environment setup involves building a Docker image as defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile). This process starts from an [`nvidia/cuda`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile#L20) base image, which provides CUDA compatibility essential for GPU acceleration. System dependencies such as Python 3.12, [`git`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/CMakeLists.txt#L22), [`gcc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile#L25), and [`make`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/LICENSE#L77) are installed, followed by the [`uv`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/pyproject.toml#L42) package manager. [`uv`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/pyproject.toml#L42) is configured to create an isolated Python virtual environment and manage AlphaFold 3's Python dependencies in a frozen and reproducible manner. HMMER version 3.4 is compiled and installed from source, including a specific patch for [`jackhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L37), highlighting the need for precise version control and customized behavior for key bioinformatics tools. The Dockerfile also integrates the AlphaFold 3 source code and executes a [`build_data`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/build_data.py#L32) script to construct necessary chemical components databases. For GPU performance optimization, XLA environment variables are explicitly configured to manage memory preallocation and general behavior, particularly for high-performance GPUs like the A100. For more detailed information on the Docker build process, refer to [Docker Image Build and Environment Setup](#setup-and-environment-configuration-docker-image-build-and-environment-setup).

Beyond the Docker image, the repository includes shell scripts in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts) to manage SSDs, particularly in cloud computing contexts like Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh) script automates the process of identifying, formatting (if necessary, using [`mkfs.ext4`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L35)), and mounting local SSDs to a specified directory, ensuring they are ready for use. Following this, the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh) script handles the transfer of large public database files to the mounted SSD. This script intelligently manages disk space by calculating the total size of files to be copied against available space and prioritizes transfers, iteratively removing less critical files if space is insufficient. This ensures that the most essential databases are moved first, optimizing data access for AlphaFold 3's operations. Further details on SSD management are available in [SSD Management for Database Storage](#setup-and-environment-configuration-ssd-management-for-database-storage).

### Docker Image Build and Environment Setup
The AlphaFold 3 Docker image is constructed to provide a reproducible and optimized environment for the model's execution. The build process, primarily defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile), starts from a CUDA-compatible base image, integrating system dependencies, Python environment management, and specialized bioinformatics tools.

Central to the Python environment setup is the [`uv`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/pyproject.toml#L42) package manager, which is installed and configured to create an isolated virtual environment. This approach ensures consistent dependency resolution and avoids conflicts with system-wide Python installations. Dependencies for AlphaFold 3 are installed using [`uv sync`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/pyproject.toml#L42) with flags that promote frozen, reproducible, and static installations.

A key bioinformatics component, HMMER (version 3.4), is compiled and installed from source. This ensures precise version control and allows for the application of specific patches, which can be crucial for the tool's performance or compatibility within the AlphaFold 3 pipeline. Following the installation of core dependencies, the Docker build process executes a [`build_data`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/build_data.py#L32) script to generate necessary chemical components databases, which are essential for the model's operation.

For performance optimization, particularly on high-performance GPUs like the A100, the Docker environment configures XLA (Accelerated Linear Algebra) flags. These settings, including [`XLA_FLAGS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L968), [`XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile#L95), and [`XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile#L96), are tuned to manage memory preallocation and optimize the acceleration of numerical computations. The overall design of the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile) emphasizes layer caching to accelerate rebuilds and uses pinned dependencies to ensure environmental stability across deployments.

### SSD Management for Database Storage
The AlphaFold 3 environment includes scripts to manage Solid State Drives (SSDs) for database storage, particularly within cloud environments such as Google Cloud Platform (GCP). These scripts facilitate the mounting, formatting, and efficient transfer of large public database files, while also addressing space constraints and prioritizing file transfers.

The primary script for configuring SSDs is [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh). This script automates the process of identifying, formatting, and mounting the first available unmounted SSD to a specified directory, which defaults to [`/mnt/disks/ssd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/installation.md#L258). It ensures idempotency, meaning it can be run multiple times without causing unintended side effects, by checking if the target mount directory is already in use. When formatting an SSD, it uses [`mkfs.ext4`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/gcp_mount_ssd.sh#L35) with options to enhance performance and manage disk space efficiently.

For transferring public database files, the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/scripts/copy_to_ssd.sh) script is utilized. This script copies a predefined list of database files from a source to a target SSD directory. It incorporates logic to handle scenarios where the available SSD space is limited. By calculating the total size of the selected files and comparing it against the available space, the script can iteratively adjust the list of files to be copied, prioritizing certain files and logging any that could not be accommodated due to insufficient space. This mechanism ensures that critical database components are transferred first, making efficient use of available storage.

## Data Parsing and Preprocessing
AlphaFold 3 processes diverse biological data formats, including Crystallographic Information File (CIF), FASTA, and Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) formats. This processing involves parsing and manipulating sequence and structure data, leveraging high-performance C++ implementations with Python bindings to ensure efficient data extraction and serialization.

For CIF data, [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc) represents data as a dictionary-like structure, capable of parsing CIF strings and serializing them back while handling complex elements such as [`data_`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L337) blocks, [`loop_`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L848) structures, and quoting rules. Python bindings for [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) enable direct manipulation of CIF data from Python, supporting conversion to NumPy arrays and dictionary-like operations.

FASTA parsing is handled by iterators defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.cc), such as [`FastaFileIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L20) and [`FastaStringIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L25). These iterators are designed for memory-efficient, lazy parsing of large FASTA files or strings, returning sequences and their descriptions incrementally. Python wrappers provide access to these iterators, allowing for efficient processing of large datasets without loading them entirely into memory.

MSA format conversion utilities, implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc), facilitate tasks such as converting A3M sequences to Stockholm format. These utilities manage sequence alignments and insertions (lowercase characters in A3M) to ensure consistent data representation for downstream modeling tasks. These C++ implementations are exposed to Python through [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) bindings, allowing AlphaFold 3 to leverage the performance of C++ for computationally intensive parsing operations while maintaining the flexibility of Python. See [C++/Python Bindings and Performance](#data-parsing-and-preprocessing-cpython-bindings-and-performance) for further details on how C++ components are integrated with Python.

### CIF Data Structures and Serialization
The AlphaFold 3 repository employs a robust C++ implementation for parsing, representing, and serializing Crystallographic Information File (CIF) data, exposed to Python through [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) bindings. This design prioritizes efficiency and seamless integration with the Python ecosystem.

The central component for handling CIF data is the [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h) and implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc). [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) represents a parsed CIF data block as a dictionary-like structure. It stores CIF fields and their associated values, managing complex aspects of the CIF format such as [`data_`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L337) blocks, key-value pairs, and [`loop_`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L848) structures. For instance, [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) can parse a CIF string into its internal representation using a static factory method [`FromString`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h#L51), and conversely, serialize itself back into a CIF-formatted string via [`ToString`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h#L54). The serialization process is sophisticated, handling quoting rules, multi-line values, and sorting keys, including a specific [`kAtomSiteSortOrder`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc#L260) for [`_atom_site`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L140) fields to maintain compatibility with PDB-standard CIF files.

To manage repetitive data often found in CIF files, [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) provides methods like [`ExtractLoopAsList`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h#L68) and [`ExtractLoopAsDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h#L83). These methods facilitate the extraction of data from CIF loops into structured Python lists of dictionaries or dictionaries of dictionaries, respectively. This allows for convenient access and manipulation of complex tabular data embedded within CIF files.

The Python bindings for [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26), found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc), expose [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) functionalities to Python. This enables Python users to initialize [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) objects from Python dictionaries, parse CIF strings, serialize to CIF strings, and convert [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) instances back into standard Python dictionaries. Crucially, the [`get_array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L92) method allows direct conversion of CIF values into NumPy arrays of specified data types, handling CIF-specific representations like [`.`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/LICENSE#L39) for [`NaN`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L805) in floats, and [`y`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L52)/[`n`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L32) or [`yes`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docker/Dockerfile#L29)/[`no`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py#L318) for booleans. This tight integration with NumPy is essential for subsequent numerical processing. The Python bindings also implement standard dictionary-like behaviors ([`__len__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L128), [`__contains__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L33), [`__getitem__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L178), [`keys`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L119), [`values`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L123), [`items`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L119)) and support Python's pickling mechanism for serialization and deserialization of [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) objects. During computationally intensive C++ operations, the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is released, as detailed in [C++/Python Bindings and Performance](#data-parsing-and-preprocessing-cpython-bindings-and-performance), allowing for concurrent Python execution and improved performance.

### Efficient FASTA Iterators
The AlphaFold 3 codebase includes C++ implementations for memory-efficient FASTA parsing, designed to handle large datasets effectively. These implementations, located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp), provide iterator-based parsing from both files and in-memory strings, enabling lazy iteration over FASTA records. This approach avoids loading entire files into memory, which is beneficial for processing extensive sequence databases.

The core functionalities are encapsulated in the [`FastaFileIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L20) and [`FastaStringIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L25) classes, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.h) and implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.cc). The [`FastaFileIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L20) facilitates sequential reading of sequence and description pairs from a specified FASTA file path, managing file streams incrementally. Similarly, the [`FastaStringIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L25) provides iterative parsing from an [`absl::string_view`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/mkdssp_pybind.cc#L44), which is useful when FASTA data is already loaded as a large string in memory. Both iterators maintain internal state to track parsing progress and yield each FASTA entry as it is processed.

To integrate these C++ efficiencies with the Python environment, [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) bindings are provided in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.cc). These bindings expose the [`FastaFileIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L20) and [`FastaStringIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L25) as Python iterator classes, allowing Python code to seamlessly iterate over FASTA records. The [`__next__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L23) method within these Python-bound iterators includes Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) release mechanisms ([`py::gil_scoped_release`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L393)), which permit other Python threads to execute concurrently during compute-intensive C++ parsing operations, thus enhancing overall application responsiveness. For in-memory string iteration, the [`PythonFastaStringIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.cc#L82) ensures the underlying string's lifetime is managed correctly to prevent data corruption. Additionally, general utilities for parsing entire FASTA strings into lists of sequences or sequence-description pairs are also exposed for convenience when full string parsing is acceptable. For more details on the C++/Python bindings, refer to [C++/Python Bindings and Performance](#data-parsing-and-preprocessing-cpython-bindings-and-performance).

### MSA Format Conversion and Alignment
The system provides C++ utilities for converting Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) data between formats, specifically from A3M to Stockholm format, and for aligning sequences to a gapless query. These functionalities are exposed to Python through [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) bindings, allowing high-performance MSA processing within a Python environment.

The [`ConvertA3MToStockholm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc#L36) function, found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc), transforms A3M-formatted sequences into Stockholm format. This conversion handles insertions (lowercase characters in A3M) by promoting them to uppercase and appropriately padding other sequences with dashes ([`-`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L75)) to maintain alignment. The function ensures consistency across sequences and raises an [`std::invalid_argument`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc#L81) error if it encounters A3M input with inconsistent row lengths.

The [`AlignSequenceToGaplessQuery`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc#L92) function, also within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc), aligns a given [`sequence`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L251) to a [`query_sequence`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L582) that is assumed to be gapless. This process identifies residues in the input [`sequence`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L251) that represent insertions relative to the query by converting them to lowercase. This is useful for tasks such as converting Stockholm MSA back to A3M format, where insertions relative to a query sequence need to be explicitly marked. A [`py::value_error`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L389) is raised if the input sequences do not have matching lengths.

These C++ functions are accessible in Python via bindings registered by [`RegisterModuleMsaConversion`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.h#L27) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc). This allows Python code to call [`convert_a3m_to_stockholm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/parsers.py#L73) and [`align_sequence_to_gapless_query`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion.pyi#L29), leveraging the performance of C++ for these critical data manipulation steps while benefiting from Python's flexibility. The bindings release the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) during C++ execution to enable concurrency and improve overall application performance. For more details on the C++/Python binding mechanisms, see [C++/Python Bindings and Performance](#data-parsing-and-preprocessing-cpython-bindings-and-performance).

### C++/Python Bindings and Performance
The AlphaFold 3 codebase utilizes [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) to create Python bindings for its high-performance C++ parsing and manipulation functionalities, particularly for CIF, FASTA, and MSA data formats. This integration allows Python-based workflows to leverage the computational efficiency of C++ for core data processing tasks.

For CIF data, [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) exposes the [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h) and implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc). This binding, detailed in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc), enables parsing CIF strings into Python-accessible dictionary-like objects and serializing them back into CIF format. A key aspect of this binding is the ability to efficiently convert CIF values into NumPy arrays through functions like [`CifDictGetArray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L282), which handles various data types, including special CIF values such as [`.`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/LICENSE#L39) (NaN) and boolean representations. This conversion is crucial for downstream numerical operations within the model.

Similarly, FASTA parsing benefits from C++ implementations exposed via [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148). The [`FastaFileIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L20) and [`FastaStringIterator`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator.pyi#L25) classes, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.h) and implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_lib.cc), allow for memory-efficient, lazy iteration over large FASTA files or strings directly from Python. The Python bindings for these iterators, found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/fasta_iterator_pybind.cc), prevent premature garbage collection of underlying data and efficiently propagate errors from C++ to Python.

MSA format conversion and sequence alignment also leverage [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) to bridge C++ and Python. Functions like [`ConvertA3MToStockholm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc#L36) and [`AlignSequenceToGaplessQuery`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc#L92), implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.cc) (with declarations in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/msa_conversion_pybind.h)), are made available in Python. These utilities handle tasks such as converting A3M sequences to Stockholm format and aligning sequences to a gapless query, which are critical steps in [Input Feature Generation](#input-feature-generation).

A common performance optimization across these bindings is the strategic use of [`py::gil_scoped_release`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L393). This mechanism ensures that the Python Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is released during computationally intensive C++ operations, allowing other Python threads to execute concurrently. This design choice enhances overall application responsiveness and throughput by preventing the GIL from becoming a bottleneck during data parsing and manipulation. Additionally, the use of [`absl::string_view`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/mkdssp_pybind.cc#L44) in the C++ layer minimizes string copying, contributing to efficient data handling.

## Input Feature Generation
The AlphaFold 3 model relies on a comprehensive process to transform raw biological data into a structured set of input features. This process involves generating Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs), identifying and extracting structural templates, and managing the overall representation of biological macromolecules. The system integrates both efficient C++ implementations and Python wrappers for external tools to achieve this.

The core of this feature generation is managed by the data processing utilities located in the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data) directory. The primary entry point for this process is [`featurise_input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py#L47) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py), which validates input data and orchestrates its transformation into [`BatchDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L52) objects suitable for model consumption. This function leverages the [`DataPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L304) class defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py) to manage the complex sequence of steps, including MSA and template generation. The pipeline utilizes a [`ThreadPoolExecutor`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L479) for parallel execution of computationally intensive tasks, allowing multiple MSA and template searches to run concurrently. To prevent redundant computations for identical sequences, especially in complexes with multiple identical chains, [`functools.cache`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L39) is used on certain pipeline steps.

Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) data is managed by the [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py). This class provides mechanisms for parsing MSAs from various formats (e.g., A3M), deduplicating sequences to ensure uniqueness, and converting raw MSA data into numerical features that capture sequence variability and deletions. The extraction of specific species identifiers from UniProtKB-formatted MSA descriptions is handled by [`get_identifiers`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_identifiers.py#L88) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_identifiers.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_identifiers.py). For performance-critical computations, such as calculating MSA profiles (residue frequencies at each position), C++ implementations are used, specifically [`ComputeMsaProfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.cc#L31) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.cc), which is exposed to Python via [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148).

The system also integrates various external tools from the HMMER suite through Python wrappers found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools). These wrappers standardize the interaction with tools like [`Jackhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L37) (for protein sequence searches, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py)), [`Nhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py#L43) (for nucleotide sequence searches, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py)), [`Hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31) (for database searches with HMM profiles, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py)), [`Hmmbuild`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L31) (for building HMM profiles, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py)), and [`Hmmalign`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L37) (for aligning sequences to HMM profiles, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py)). These wrappers handle details such as sharded database searches, temporary file management, and consistent parsing of tool outputs, abstracting away the complexities of command-line execution. An [`MsaTool`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py#L44) protocol in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py) provides a standardized interface for all MSA tools.

Structural template handling is managed by the [`Templates`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L719) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py). This class collects potential structural matches (hits) from searches, filters them based on various criteria (e.g., release date, alignment quality, sequence identity), and then featurizes them into model-ready inputs. A notable aspect of template processing is the [`realign_hit_to_structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/template_realign.py#L29) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/template_realign.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/template_realign.py), which addresses discrepancies between sequences obtained from template search tools (often derived from PDB SEQRES records) and the actual sequences in mmCIF structures, ensuring accurate mapping for feature generation. Structures are retrieved from various sources using the [`StructureStore`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/structure_stores.py#L32) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/structure_stores.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/structure_stores.py), which supports in-memory mappings, tar archives, or filesystem directories.

For handling molecular data beyond proteins and nucleic acids, particularly ligands, the [`rdkit_utils`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L38) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py) provides utilities for converting molecular data between RDKit [`Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L796) objects and CCD-like mmCIF dictionaries. This includes parsing atom and bond data, populating molecular structures, and generating 3D conformers for molecules, which are essential for ligand featurization. This integration ensures that the AlphaFold 3 model can process a diverse range of biological entities. For a detailed discussion on how these features are consumed by the model, see [Core Model Architecture and Pipeline](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline).

### Featurization Pipeline and Data Orchestration
The featurization pipeline in AlphaFold 3 processes raw biological data into a structured format suitable for model inference. This process begins with [`validate_fold_input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py#L33) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py), which ensures the integrity of input data ([`folding_input.Input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L566)) by checking for required fields such as unpaired Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs), paired MSAs, and templates for protein chains, or unpaired MSAs for RNA chains. The primary function for orchestrating this conversion is [`featurise_input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py#L47), also in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py). This function converts the validated [`folding_input.Input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L566) into [`features.BatchDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L480) objects. It supports the generation of multiple featurized batches by processing data with different random seeds, which can be valuable for ensemble predictions or robust analysis.

The [`featurise_input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/featurisation.py#L47) function leverages the [`DataPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L304) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py), to manage the computationally intensive tasks of MSA and template generation. The [`DataPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L304) orchestrates these processes in parallel using thread pools, making the data preparation efficient. For proteins, it generates MSAs using tools like Jackhmmer and performs template searches with Hmmsearch against various databases. For RNA chains, it generates MSAs using Nhmmer against RNA-specific databases. The pipeline intelligently skips searches if the required data is already present in the input. After these tools run, the [`DataPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L304) aggregates the results (MSAs and templates) into a structured format ready for the AlphaFold model. The [`DataPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L304) uses configurations defined in [`msa_config.RunConfig`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L333) and [`msa_config.TemplatesConfig`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L44) to control parameters for each specific MSA and template search tool, including database details, E-values, and CPU usage. This modular and configurable design allows for flexible setup and execution of the featurization process.

### Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) Management and Feature Extraction
Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) management in AlphaFold 3 involves the structured representation, manipulation, and featurization of MSA data, crucial for providing the model with evolutionary information. The central component for this is the [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py). This class acts as a container for MSA sequences and their associated descriptions, ensuring consistency by verifying that all sequences originate from the same query and polymer type.

The [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) class supports initialization from various sources. It can be constructed directly from A3M-formatted strings via methods like [`from_a3m`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L208) and [`from_multiple_a3ms`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L165), or by merging existing [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) objects using [`from_multiple_msas`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L122). For cases where no external MSA is available, an empty [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) containing only the query sequence can be created with [`from_empty`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L238). A key aspect of [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) management is deduplication, which occurs during initialization and through dedicated methods. This process specifically handles lowercase characters, treating them as insertions that should be ignored when identifying unique sequences.

The conversion of raw MSA data into numerical features suitable for the model is handled by the [`featurize`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L263) method of the [`Msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61) class. This method leverages helper functions in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_features.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_features.py) to extract features such as the numerical representation of sequences ([`msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L61)), a matrix quantifying deletions ([`deletion_matrix`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L417)), and species identifiers. The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_features.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_features.py) module includes specific character mappings for protein, RNA, and DNA residues, and uses regular expressions to parse UniProtKB-formatted descriptions to extract species IDs. These species IDs are then encapsulated in an [`Identifiers`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_identifiers.py#L55) dataclass, as defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_identifiers.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_identifiers.py).

For computationally intensive tasks like MSA profile computation, AlphaFold 3 utilizes high-performance C++ implementations. The [`ComputeMsaProfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.cc#L31) function, located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.cc), calculates a residue frequency profile from an integer-encoded MSA. This profile indicates the frequency of each residue type at every position in the MSA, normalized by the MSA depth. This C++ functionality is exposed to Python through [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) via the [`RegisterModuleMsaProfile`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/cpp/msa_profile_pybind.h#L27) function, allowing Python components to benefit from the speed of C++ for this specific task. The configuration for MSA tools, including external search tools like Jackhmmer and Nhmmer, is managed through dataclasses defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_config.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_config.py), allowing for flexible parameter settings for database paths, CPU usage, and various statistical thresholds. External tools themselves are wrapped in Python classes as described in [HMMER Suite Wrappers for MSA and Template Search](#input-feature-generation-hmmer-suite-wrappers-for-msa-and-template-search).

### HMMER Suite Wrappers for MSA and Template Search
Python wrappers provide an interface to the HMMER suite of tools, which are used for sequence and profile-based searches against biological sequence databases. These wrappers standardize interactions with various Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) tools and manage searches against sharded databases. The common interface for these tools is defined by the [`MsaTool`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py#L44) protocol and the [`MsaToolResult`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py#L27) dataclass in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/msa_tool.py).

The [`Hmmbuild`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L31) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py) provides a wrapper for the [`hmmbuild`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L31) binary. It constructs HMM profiles from MSAs provided in Stockholm or A3M formats. For A3M input, it preprocesses the MSA by removing inserted residues to convert it into an aligned FASTA format before profile construction.

The [`Hmmalign`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L37) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py) wraps the [`hmmalign`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L37) binary to align sequences to an HMM profile. It handles input sequences in A3M format and preprocesses them by removing gaps and converting to uppercase to prepare them for alignment.

For searching sequence databases with HMM profiles, the [`Hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py) wraps the [`hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31) binary. It supports querying directly with a pre-built HMM or by first building an HMM from an A3M or Stockholm MSA using an internal [`hmmbuild`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L31) instance. The output from [`hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31) (in Stockholm format) is converted to A3M format.

The [`Jackhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L37) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py) provides a wrapper for the [`jackhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L37) binary. It performs iterative sequence searches against protein sequence databases and generates MSAs. It supports sharded databases, executing queries in parallel across shards and merging results based on e-values and bit scores. Result merging is an important aspect of managing sharded databases, ensuring that top hits are consistently identified across all shards.

Similarly, the [`Nhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py#L43) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py) wraps the [`Nhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/nhmmer.py#L43) binary for searching nucleotide sequence databases. Like [`Jackhmmer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/jackhmmer.py#L37), it supports sharded databases, using parallel execution for shards and merging results. It also includes post-processing steps using [`Hmmalign`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L37) and [`Hmmbuild`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmbuild.py#L31) to ensure MSA width consistency with the query sequence. Special handling is implemented for short RNA sequences by adjusting parameters.

Throughout these wrappers, temporary files are used for input and output. External command execution, logging, and error management are handled by functions such as [`run`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/subprocess_utils.py#L67), ensuring robust interaction with the underlying HMMER binaries. For managing sharded database paths, the [`shards`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L54) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/shards.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/shards.py) provides utilities to parse shard specifications and generate lists of sharded file paths.

### Template Retrieval, Filtering, and Realignment
Structural templates play a crucial role in the AlphaFold 3 prediction pipeline by providing existing structural information that can guide the model. The system manages the retrieval, filtering, and featurization of these templates to ensure high-quality and relevant structural data is used as input.

Template retrieval often begins with sequence searches against structural databases. The system leverages HMMER suite tools such as [`hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31) to identify potential structural homologs. For instance, [`hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31) can be executed by [`run_hmmsearch_with_a3m`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L968) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py), using an input Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) to query a database and produce a list of template candidates. These candidates, or "hits," are encapsulated in [`Hit`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L167) objects defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py). Each [`Hit`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L167) stores critical metadata, including the PDB ID, chain ID, sequences, and release date, as well as alignment information.

Once potential templates are identified, they undergo a rigorous filtering process. The [`filter`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L610) method of the [`Templates`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L719) class, located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py), applies various criteria defined in [`msa_config.TemplateFilterConfig`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/pipeline.py#L459) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_config.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa_config.py). These filters include checking for maximum subsequence ratios, minimum alignment ratios, minimum hit lengths, and ensuring that templates are not too recent based on a [`release_date_cutoff`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py#L598). Duplicate sequences are also removed to prevent redundancy. This step ensures that only the most relevant and reliable templates are passed on for featurization.

A significant challenge in using structural templates is reconciling discrepancies between sequences obtained from sequence databases (like those used by [`hmmsearch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmsearch.py#L31), which often rely on PDB SEQRES records) and the actual sequences present in the mmCIF structural files. The [`realign_hit_to_structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/template_realign.py#L29) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/template_realign.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/template_realign.py) addresses this by adjusting the mapping from the query sequence to the precise structural sequence. It iteratively attempts to realign the template hit sequence with the mmCIF structure sequence, accounting for potential insertions or deletions. This process helps to generate an accurate mapping, ensuring that the model's input features correctly reflect the true structural context.

Finally, the filtered and realigned template hits are featurized. The [`featurize`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/msa.py#L263) method in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/templates.py) extracts structural and sequence features for both polymer chains and ligands from the selected [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects (see [Molecular Structure Management](#molecular-structure-management)). These features include atomic positions, masks, sequence identity, and amino acid types. These extracted features are then packaged into a structured format suitable for consumption by the AlphaFold 3 model.

### RDKit Utilities for Molecular Data and Conformer Generation
The [`rdkit_utils`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L38) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py) provides functionalities for managing and converting molecular data, particularly between RDKit [`Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L796) objects and Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD)-like mmCIF dictionaries. This is crucial for enabling AlphaFold 3 to work with diverse chemical entities such as ligands.

The primary conversion functions are [`mol_from_ccd_cif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L164) and [`mol_to_ccd_cif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L254). The [`mol_from_ccd_cif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L164) function ingests molecular data from a [`cif_dict.CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L1506) (which represents an entry from the CCD database) and constructs an RDKit [`Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L796) object. This process involves extracting atom-specific data like names, types, and charges, as well as bond data including connectivity and order. To manage imperfect or incomplete input data, [`mol_from_ccd_cif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L164) includes a [`force_parse`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L152) option, allowing the system to handle missing or non-standard values gracefully. Once the molecular structure is populated, the function can attempt to add 3D coordinates from the mmCIF data, if available, and assign stereochemistry. It also performs sanitization checks and can optionally sort atoms alphabetically or remove hydrogens. Conversely, [`mol_to_ccd_cif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L254) translates an RDKit [`Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L796) object back into a [`cif_dict.CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L1506) format, ensuring that atom names are assigned and populating [`_chem_comp_atom`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L849) and [`_chem_comp_bond`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L879) categories with detailed atom and bond information.

Beyond conversions, the module also supports the generation of 3D conformers. The [`get_random_conformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L534) function uses RDKit's ETKDGv3 algorithm to generate a 3D conformer for a molecule, which is essential when coordinate data might be absent from the input. This capability ensures that molecular structures can be provided with a reasonable 3D representation for downstream modeling tasks.

## Molecular Structure Management
AlphaFold 3 represents and processes molecular structures using a robust and immutable data model built on typed NumPy arrays. This system facilitates structural analysis, manipulation, and filtering, ensuring data consistency. The core data structure for a molecular entity is the [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py), which aggregates chains, residues, atoms, and bonds. These components are themselves dataclasses that store their properties as NumPy arrays, enabling efficient, array-based operations.

The system provides functionalities for parsing various structural data formats into the [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) representation. [`from_mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L408) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py) parses mmCIF files from strings, while [`from_parsed_mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L316) handles already parsed mmCIF objects. These functions are critical for converting raw structural data into a standardized [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) format, including the handling of data fixes and bond information. Low-level mmCIF parsing utilities are available in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py), which wraps C++-backed functionality for robustness.

Beyond basic parsing, the system manages specialized structural information such as biological assemblies and chemical components. The [`BioassemblyData`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L84) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py) handles parsing, storing, and applying bioassembly transformations defined in mmCIF files, enabling the reconstruction of biological assemblies. Chemical component data, detailing information about chemical compounds, their atoms, and bonds, is processed by [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py). This includes utilities to parse, represent, and manipulate these components, crucial for accurate molecular representation.

Performance-critical operations are optimized using C++ implementations exposed to Python via Pybind11. The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp) directory contains these implementations, which cover tasks such as mmCIF alt-loc resolution (selecting a single atomic conformation from multiple possibilities based on occupancy), efficient membership testing of [`int64_t`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_pybind.cc#L177) elements from NumPy arrays against a set of values, and optimized operations for NumPy object and string arrays. These C++ extensions enhance the efficiency of data processing and manipulation within the molecular structure management framework.

### Core Data Structures for Molecular Representation
The molecular structure management in AlphaFold 3 centers around a robust, immutable data model designed for efficiency and consistency. The [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py), serves as the primary representation of a molecular entity. It aggregates data for chains, residues, atoms, and bonds, storing them as instances of specialized [`dataclasses`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L33): [`Chains`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L114), [`Residues`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py#L214), [`Atoms`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py#L89) (from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py)), and [`Bonds`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bonds.py#L33) (from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bonds.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bonds.py)). These dataclasses extend a common [`Table`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L58) base class, implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py).

The [`Table`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L58) base class provides a dataclass-based, immutable structure that underpins the storage of structural data. Each [`Table`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L58) instance manages columns of equal length, identified by a unique [`key`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.cc#L322), with all data columns backed by [`numpy.ndarray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership.pyi#L24) objects. This [`numpy.ndarray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership.pyi#L24) backend is crucial for enabling efficient, vectorized operations across the structural data. The design emphasizes immutability; any operation that conceptually "modifies" a [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) or its constituent tables actually returns a *new* instance with the desired changes, promoting predictable behavior and simplifying data integrity.

Data consistency is maintained through several mechanisms. The [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) class enforces foreign key relationships between its internal tables, ensuring that, for example, an atom always belongs to an existing residue, and a residue to an existing chain. This relational integrity is validated during object construction using [`_validate_table_foreign_keys`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L355). Furthermore, the [`_cascade_delete`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L1426) mechanism within the [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) class ensures that when a higher-level entity (like a residue) is removed, all its dependent lower-level entities (like its atoms) are also appropriately handled, preventing orphaned records and maintaining structural coherence. This immutable, table-based design, coupled with [`numpy.ndarray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership.pyi#L24) for core data storage, provides a powerful and efficient framework for representing and manipulating molecular structures within AlphaFold 3. The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure) directory provides a consolidated interface for accessing these core structural components.

### mmCIF Parsing and Data Ingestion
Parsing and ingesting mmCIF files into the AlphaFold 3 [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) representation involves a tiered approach, utilizing both high-level Python utilities and performance-optimized C++ backends. The central module for creating [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects from various inputs is [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py). This module acts as the primary interface, allowing the construction of [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) objects from mmCIF strings, pre-parsed [`mmcif.Mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L171) objects, residue-level arrays, or atom-level arrays. It incorporates functionalities for handling specific data fixes, such as normalizing selenomethionine (MSE) residues to methionine (MET), correcting arginine atom ordering, and identifying unknown DNA residues.

At a lower level, the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py) module provides fundamental utilities for interacting with mmCIF data. This includes functions for converting between integer and string chain IDs, parsing multi-data mmCIF strings, and extracting specific metadata such as experimental method, release date, and resolution. A key capability is the parsing of [`oper_expression`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L261) fields, which describe symmetry operations crucial for reconstructing biological assemblies. This module wraps C++-backed functionalities for performance-critical operations, ensuring efficient parsing and data extraction.

The C++ implementations, found within the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp) directory, are exposed to Python via [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) and significantly enhance parsing efficiency. For example, [`mmcif_altlocs`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.cc#L20) handles the resolution of alternate location groups in mmCIF data, selecting the most probable atomic conformation based on occupancy. [`mmcif_atom_site_pybind`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/cpp.cc#L28) assists in inferring atom type symbols and mapping internal to author chain IDs, while [`mmcif_struct_conn_pybind`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/cpp.cc#L30) extracts bond information from mmCIF [`_struct_conn`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L144) tables. Additionally, [`mmcif_layout_pybind`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/cpp.cc#L29) provides an [`MmcifLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h#L37) class for efficiently managing the structural hierarchy of parsed mmCIF files. These C++ components collectively accelerate data ingestion and ensure data integrity.

The overall process ensures that raw mmCIF data is not only parsed but also normalized and cleaned before being converted into the robust [`Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) data model. This robust representation, which uses [`dataclasses`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L33) with [`numpy.ndarray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership.pyi#L24) backends for efficient operations, is further detailed in [Core Data Structures for Molecular Representation](#molecular-structure-management-core-data-structures-for-molecular-representation). Utilities such as [`_generate_required_tables_if_missing`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L1019) dynamically infer and populate crucial mmCIF categories if they are absent, enhancing robustness against diverse mmCIF sources. The comprehensive handling of chemical component data, including parsing and serialization, is managed through the classes defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py) and is essential for accurately representing both standard and non-standard molecular moieties. See [Handling Bioassemblies and Chemical Components](#molecular-structure-management-handling-bioassemblies-and-chemical-components) for more information.

### Handling Bioassemblies and Chemical Components
AlphaFold 3 represents and manages molecular structures, including specialized handling for biological assembly information and chemical component data. The data structures and parsing mechanisms for biological assemblies are defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py). The [`BioassemblyData`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L84) class stores and processes information related to macromolecular complexes from mmCIF files. It utilizes [`Operation`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L32) dataclasses to represent individual rigid transformations (rotation and translation) and [`Transform`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L44) dataclasses to define sequences of these operations that are applied to specific chains. The [`BioassemblyData.from_mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L293) method parses this information from an [`mmcif.Mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L171) object, extracting details such as [`_pdbx_struct_assembly_gen`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L96) to determine how different chains are transformed to form an assembly. The [`get_transforms`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L231) method then generates a sequence of [`Transform`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/bioassemblies.py#L44) objects, handling chain ID renaming to ensure unique identifiers for all transformed copies of chains within an assembly. This allows for the reconstruction of full biological assemblies from the asymmetric unit coordinates.

Similarly, AlphaFold 3 incorporates robust management of chemical component data, which describes the properties of individual chemical compounds, including their atoms and bonds. This functionality is primarily implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py). The core data structures include [`ChemCompAtom`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py#L47) and [`ChemCompBond`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py#L72), which represent atoms and bonds within a chemical component, respectively.
