These are aggregated into [`ChemCompEntry`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py#L93) objects, which encapsulate all information for a single chemical component, such as its name, formula, and SMILES string. A collection of these entries is managed by the [`ChemicalComponentsData`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/chemical_components.py#L142) class. The [`ChemicalComponentsData.from_mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L299) method parses chemical component definitions directly from mmCIF files, while [`to_mmcif_dict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L2952) facilitates serialization back into mmCIF format. This module can also retrieve and populate missing chemical component data from a Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD), ensuring comprehensive representation of both standard and non-standard chemical entities within a structure. This detailed management of both bioassembly and chemical component data enables a comprehensive understanding and manipulation of complex molecular systems. For more on the foundational data structures of molecules, refer to [Core Data Structures for Molecular Representation](#molecular-structure-management-core-data-structures-for-molecular-representation).

### Performance-Critical C++ Implementations (Pybind11)
The [`cpp`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L139) subdirectory within the [`structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L306) module provides C++ implementations, exposed via [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148), for performance-critical operations involved in processing and managing molecular structure data. These functionalities are crucial for handling large [`mmCIF`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L38) files efficiently and preparing data for downstream modeling tasks.

One key area is the efficient management of structural hierarchy. The [`MmcifLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h#L37) class in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_lib.cc) parses the [`_atom_site`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L140) records of an [`mmCIF`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L38) file to provide a structured view of models, chains, residues, and atoms. This layout allows for quick identification of atom and residue ranges for specific chains, and its C++ implementation ensures that queries on the structural organization are performed with optimal speed. The [`MmcifLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h#L37) can also be filtered to retain only specific residues, and it can be constructed from [`CifDict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict.pyi#L26) objects, with robust error handling for inconsistent or malformed data. The Python bindings for [`MmcifLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout.h#L37) are provided in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_pybind.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_layout_pybind.cc), allowing Python users to leverage this efficient data structure for structural queries.

Another critical function is the resolution of alternate locations (alt-locs) in [`mmCIF`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L38) data. The [`ResolveMmcifAltLocs`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.h#L49) function, implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_altlocs.cc), ensures that each atom has a unique spatial representation by selecting the most appropriate atom record when multiple alt-locs are present. This process prioritizes higher occupancy and uses alphabetical order for tie-breaking, ensuring a deterministic and chemically sensible selection. This functionality is essential for preparing clean, unambiguous structural data.

Efficient array operations are also vital for performance. The [`cpp`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L139) directory includes optimized C++ implementations for common NumPy array manipulations, particularly for arrays containing Python objects and strings. For instance, the [`IsIn`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.cc#L35) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.cc) offers an O(N) complexity for membership testing, which is faster than NumPy's [`np.isin`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L978) for large datasets. Similarly, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc) provides [`RemapNumpyArrayObjects`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc#L50) for remapping array elements based on a dictionary, [`FormatFloatArray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc#L140) for efficient float-to-string conversion, and [`RemapMultipleArrays`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.cc#L183) for consolidating data from multiple arrays. These C++ implementations, exposed through [`pybind11`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L148) ([`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/membership_pybind.h), [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/string_array_pybind.h)), minimize Python overhead and accelerate data preprocessing.

The extraction of bond information from [`mmCIF`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L38) files is handled by [`GetBondAtomIndices`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn.h#L37) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn.h) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_lib.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_lib.cc). This function parses the [`_struct_conn`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L144) table to identify bonds and maps them to 0-based atom indices within the [`_atom_site`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L140) table. It also includes specific workarounds for known PDB data anomalies, ensuring robust bond extraction even from imperfect data. The Python binding ([`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_pybind.h`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_pybind.h), [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_struct_conn_pybind.cc)) allows Python code to retrieve this critical connectivity information.

Finally, the [`mmcif_utils`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/cpp.cc#L46) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_utils_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/cpp/mmcif_utils_pybind.cc) provides further Python bindings for C++ utilities that process and manipulate [`mmCIF`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L38) structural data. This includes functions for filtering atoms based on entity types (e.g., nucleotides, ligands, water) and for applying in-place corrections to residue-specific atom properties, such as fixing Arginine residues. These utilities help in cleaning and standardizing input data before it is fed into the AlphaFold 3 model.

## Core Model Architecture and Pipeline
The AlphaFold 3 model's architecture integrates several components, from processing initial input features to predicting molecular structures and scoring their confidence. The overall model is implemented in the [`Model`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L225) class within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py). This class orchestrates the conversion of input data into a feature batch, refines embeddings using an Evoformer, samples atom positions through a diffusion head, and calculates confidence scores and distogram predictions.

A crucial aspect of the pipeline involves converting raw macromolecular entities, typically from mmCIF files, into model-ready feature objects. This is managed by the [`WholePdbPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L86) class located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py). This pipeline includes several steps such as cleaning the input structure by removing non-standard atoms, water, and hydrogens. It also identifies and processes inter-chain bonds between polymers and ligands or between ligands themselves, which is essential for understanding molecular interactions. The pipeline then tokenizes atoms into units suitable for the model and generates a diverse set of features, including Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA), template information, and reference structures. Data padding is applied to ensure consistent input dimensions for batch processing. For more details on the transformation of raw biological data into model-ready inputs, refer to [Macromolecular Data Processing Pipeline](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-macromolecular-data-processing-pipeline).

The neural network's backbone is defined within the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network) directory. This includes architectures such as the Evoformer and Pairformer, which are responsible for refining sequence and pair embeddings. These modules incorporate information like relative position encodings, bond details, and template features. Atom-level cross-attention mechanisms are also employed, which are critical for integrating atom-specific information. The model leverages a diffusion denoising process, implemented in the [`DiffusionHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L110) within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py), to iteratively sample and refine atom positions, ultimately leading to structure generation. These core network components are further elaborated in [Core Network Architectures](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-core-network-architectures).

Beyond structure prediction, AlphaFold 3 also provides mechanisms for assessing the quality and reliability of its predictions. Confidence scoring modules, found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py), predict metrics such as predicted distance errors (PDE), predicted aligned errors (PAE), and predicted lDDT. These modules are crucial for evaluating the accuracy of the structural models. Utilities for structural analysis, like clash detection and solvent accessibility calculations, further aid in post-processing and validating model outputs. See [Confidence Scoring and Structural Analysis Utilities](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-confidence-scoring-and-structural-analysis-utilities) for a deeper dive into these features.

The model also utilizes various Haiku modules, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py), such as custom [`LayerNorm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py#L50) and [`Linear`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py#L197) layers, designed for numerical stability and mixed-precision training. Utilities for sharded mapping, located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py), manage memory and throughput by processing data in smaller chunks. These components are vital for optimizing model performance and resource utilization. Additional details on these can be found in [Haiku Modules and Optimization Utilities](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-haiku-modules-and-optimization-utilities).
The output of the model, including structural predictions and confidence metrics, is then processed and saved using functionalities in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py). This step also involves adding ModelCIF-compliant metadata to the generated mmCIF files to ensure data provenance and quality reporting, as detailed in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/mmcif_metadata.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/mmcif_metadata.py). For efficient serialization of complex confidence data, C++ implementations are exposed to Python using Pybind11, as seen in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/json_serialize_pybind.cc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/json_serialize_pybind.cc).

### Macromolecular Data Processing Pipeline
The AlphaFold 3 model relies on a structured pipeline to convert raw macromolecular data, typically sourced from mmCIF files, into model-ready feature objects. This process, primarily managed by the [`WholePdbPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L86) class located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py), involves several stages: cleaning the input structures, identifying inter-chain bonds, tokenizing atoms, generating a variety of features, and finally padding the data for efficient batch processing.

The pipeline begins with a cleaning phase, where raw [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects are refined. This involves removing non-standard atoms, water molecules, and hydrogens. These operations ensure that the downstream model receives only relevant and standardized atomic information. This cleaning process is configured through various flags that allow for flexibility in how structures are prepared, such as enforcing covalent bonds or removing specific "leaving atoms" that might be part of glycan structures. This step uses functionalities within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/structure_cleaning.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/structure_cleaning.py).

Following cleaning, the pipeline identifies and extracts inter-molecular bonds. This is crucial for understanding how different chains (e.g., polymers and ligands) interact within a complex. The system uses specific logic to differentiate between inter-residue bonds in ligands and inter-chain bonds in other contexts, allowing for precise identification of interactions such as polymer-ligand and ligand-ligand bonds. The identification process is handled by functions in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/inter_chain_bonds.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/inter_chain_bonds.py), which supports filtering by chain type, residue name, and bond distance.

The cleaned and bond-identified structures are then subjected to atom tokenization. In this step, the atomic layout is converted into "tokens," which can represent residues or individual atoms, particularly for ligands. This tokenized representation is a fundamental unit for the downstream model's processing.

With the basic structural information prepared, the pipeline proceeds to generate a comprehensive set of features. This includes various feature types derived from the Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) and structural templates, as well as atom-specific and token-specific features. Features related to inter-molecular bonds, pseudo-beta atom information, and structural frames are also computed. Each type of feature is generated by dedicated modules, contributing to the rich input representation required by AlphaFold 3. For further details on MSA and template generation, refer to [Input Feature Generation](#input-feature-generation).

Finally, to optimize model training and inference, the generated features are padded. This involves adjusting the size of the input data to fit predefined buckets, ensuring that batches of data have consistent dimensions. This padding mechanism minimizes computational overhead by reducing the need for dynamic memory allocation and frequent model recompilations during batch processing.

#### Structure Cleaning and Inter-Chain Bond Identification
Raw [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects undergo a cleaning process within the data pipeline to prepare them for featurization and model input. This involves removing elements not relevant to the modeling task or those that could introduce noise. The [`clean_structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/structure_cleaning.py#L75) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/structure_cleaning.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/structure_cleaning.py) orchestrates these operations. This includes filtering out non-standard atoms, water molecules, and hydrogen atoms. Chains without specified sequences can also be dropped. A more complex cleaning step involves the removal of "leaving atoms," such as those associated with amino acid termini (e.g., OXT, HXT) or specific atoms in glycans, to ensure the structural representation is consistent. The process can also enforce the use of only covalent bonds and identify and remove "bad bonds" based on distance thresholds or polymer-polymer interactions.

Following structure cleaning, the pipeline identifies and processes inter-chain bonds, which are critical for understanding how different molecular components interact. The module [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/inter_chain_bonds.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/inter_chain_bonds.py) provides functions like [`get_polymer_ligand_bonds`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/inter_chain_bonds.py#L171) and [`get_ligand_ligand_bonds`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/inter_chain_bonds.py#L135) to specifically extract bonds between polymers and ligands, and between different ligands, respectively. These functions filter bonds based on criteria such as chain type, residue name, bond type, and maximum bond distance. The bond information is then represented in an [`atom_layout.AtomLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L93) object, detailing the atoms involved in each bond. If configured, the system also handles cases where an atom might be involved in multiple bonds, ensuring a consistent representation. The overall process, managed by the [`WholePdbPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L86) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py), consolidates these cleaned structures and identified bonds with other generated features into a [`feat_batch.Batch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L80) object, which is then ready for model consumption. For further details on the broader context of data processing, refer to the [Macromolecular Data Processing Pipeline](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-macromolecular-data-processing-pipeline) section.

#### Atom Layout and Feature Generation
Atomic and residue information is managed and transformed into [`AtomLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L45) objects as a foundational step in preparing input for the AlphaFold 3 model. This process begins with the [`WholePdbPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L86) which tokenizes the cleaned structural data. Tokenization, influenced by configuration options such as [`max_atoms_per_token`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L141) and [`flatten_non_standard_residues`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L155), converts the atom layout into the basic units (e.g., residues or individual ligand atoms) that the model processes.

The [`AtomLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L45) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py), serves as a structured representation for atom-level properties, storing details such as [`atom_name`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L570), [`res_id`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L544), and [`chain_id`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L534). Similarly, the [`Residues`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py#L214) dataclass, also in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py), holds residue-level metadata like [`res_name`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L548) and [`chain_type`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L539). These dataclasses ensure immutability and consistency, providing a reliable foundation for downstream operations. The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py) module also provides utility functions to convert raw [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects into [`AtomLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L45) and [`Residues`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py#L214) instances, inferring details like termini and deprotonation states. This includes a robust mechanism for generating a flat [`AtomLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L45) from [`Residues`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py#L214) objects, optionally incorporating hydrogens and handling unknown residues using chemical component definitions and RDKit utilities for SMILES-based atom generation.

Following this initial structuring, various feature modules generate model inputs. These include features for [`AtomCrossAtt`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L1910), [`TokenFeatures`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L905), [`MSA`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L412), [`Templates`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L719), and bond information, all coordinated by the [`WholePdbPipeline`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L86). For instance, [`MSA.compute_features`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L339) handles multiple sequence alignment data, while [`Templates.compute_features`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L351) processes structural templates. Information regarding polymer-ligand and ligand-ligand bonds is generated by dedicated features within the pipeline. Each feature module is responsible for computing a specific set of inputs for the model.

Finally, all generated features are padded to uniform sizes and assembled into a [`feat_batch.Batch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L80) object. This padding, managed by the [`calculate_bucket_size`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/pipeline/pipeline.py#L43) function within the pipeline, is crucial for efficient batch processing and memory management during model inference and training. The [`GatherInfo`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L314) dataclass and its associated [`compute_gather_idxs`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L894) and [`convert`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py#L218) functions are used to efficiently remap and transform data between different [`AtomLayout`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/atom_layout/atom_layout.py#L45) representations. This ensures data consistency and optimal performance as features are passed through the model.

### Core Network Architectures
The core network architectures in AlphaFold 3 are primarily responsible for refining molecular representations and generating new structures. This involves three main components: the Evoformer/Pairformer for refining sequence and pairwise embeddings, atom-level cross-attention mechanisms for detailed atomic interactions, and a generative diffusion denoising process for structure prediction. These components are implemented using Haiku modules and JAX for efficient computation.

The [`Evoformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L39) module, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py), processes diverse input features to generate and refine 'single' (per-residue) and 'pair' (pairwise interaction) embeddings. It integrates relative position information, chemical bond data, structural template features, and Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) derived features. The [`_relative_encoding`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L86) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py) generates features based on the relative positions of tokens and residues, including chain and symmetry identifiers. Bond information is incorporated by [`_embed_bonds`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L129) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py), which creates a contact matrix from polymer-ligand and ligand-ligand bond data. Template features are embedded by [`_embed_template_pair`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L180) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py), leveraging the [`TemplateEmbedding`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/template_modules.py#L118) module from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/template_modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/template_modules.py) to process structural templates. MSA features are processed through [`_embed_process_msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L209) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py), which uses modules such as [`EvoformerIteration`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L542) and [`PairFormerIteration`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L422) from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py) for iterative refinement. The [`PairFormerIteration`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L422) block, central to both the Evoformer and the final refinement stages, applies operations like [`TriangleMultiplication`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L254) and [`GridSelfAttention`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L140) to iteratively update both single and pair representations.

Atom-level cross-attention mechanisms, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py), are used to encode and decode atomic information. The [`atom_cross_att_encoder`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L126) processes initial atom features and conditions them with [`trunk_single_cond`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L169) and [`trunk_pair_cond`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L170), which represent higher-level single and pair conditioning information. It utilizes [`atom_layout.convert`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model.py#L98) to efficiently manage data transformations between different atom representations. This encoder aggregates atom-level information into token features. Conversely, the [`atom_cross_att_decoder`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L370) takes token-level activations and decodes them back into atom position updates, using information from the encoder and refined conditioning. Both the encoder and decoder rely on [`diffusion_transformer.CrossAttTransformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L37) from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py) for their core attention mechanisms, enabling interactions between atom-level queries and key features.

The generative diffusion denoising process, managed by the [`DiffusionHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L110) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py), is responsible for predicting atomic coordinates. This module takes noisy atom positions and iteratively denoises them to generate a stable structure. The [`_conditioning`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L143) method within [`DiffusionHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L110) prepares [`single_cond`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L178) and [`pair_cond`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L116) embeddings by incorporating various features and noise level embeddings from [`noise_level_embeddings.noise_embeddings`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L189) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/noise_level_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/noise_level_embeddings.py). The denoising process integrates the atom-level cross-attention encoder and decoder for detailed atomic processing, along with a [`diffusion_transformer.Transformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L128) from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py) for token-level refinement. The [`sample`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L306) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py) orchestrates the iterative generation of structures from initial noise, applying rigid augmentations and following a specific noise schedule.

The underlying transformer components, detailed in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py), provide adaptive mechanisms for normalization and initialization. Functions like [`adaptive_layernorm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L32) and [`adaptive_zero_init`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L63) allow the network to dynamically adjust its operations based on contextual information. Both self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms are implemented with support for pair conditioning, using [`jax.nn.softmax`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L117) for attention weights and optional gating for information flow. The [`Transformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L189) and [`CrossAttTransformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py#L340) classes stack these components to build complex models, often leveraging [`hk.experimental.layer_stack`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L244) for managing deep networks.

#### Evoformer and Pairformer for Embedding Refinement
The [`Evoformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L39) architecture, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py), refines representations of protein sequences and structures through an iterative process. It takes initial embeddings and integrates various biological features to produce refined "single" (per-residue) and "pair" (residue-pair) representations that capture complex interactions.

The [`Evoformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L39) operates by sequentially incorporating different types of information. It begins by generating initial pair representations from target sequence features. It then integrates relative positional encodings, which capture spatial relationships between residues based on their positions within the sequence and chain. Bond information, derived from polymer-ligand and ligand-ligand interactions, is also embedded into the pair representations.

A significant component of the [`Evoformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L39) is its use of template information. Structural templates, which are existing protein structures similar to the target, are processed by modules such as [`TemplateEmbedding`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/template_modules.py#L118) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/template_modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/template_modules.py). This process generates a fixed-size embedding that provides structural context, incorporating distogram features (binned inter-residue distances) and backbone rigid body information. This template embedding is then added to the pair representations.

Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) features are crucial for capturing evolutionary information. The [`Evoformer`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L39) processes MSA data, which includes one-hot encodings of residue types and deletion information generated by functions like [`featurization.create_msa_feat`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L221) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/featurization.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/featurization.py). This MSA information, after being potentially shuffled and truncated by utilities such as [`featurization.shuffle_msa`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L219) and [`featurization.truncate_msa_batch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/evoformer.py#L220), is processed through an [`EvoformerIteration`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L542) stack, which updates both MSA and pair representations.

Finally, both the single and pair representations undergo iterative refinement through a stack of [`PairFormerIteration`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L422) blocks, implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py). These blocks employ various operations, including [`TriangleMultiplication`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L254) for combining pairwise activations, and [`GridSelfAttention`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L140) for computing attention across different dimensions of the representations. This iterative refinement allows for continuous communication and integration of information between the single and pair representations, enhancing their quality and predictive power. The architecture benefits from modular configuration and Haiku modules for flexible and efficient neural network construction, with support for bfloat16 precision for performance optimization.

#### Atom-Level Cross-Attention and Diffusion Denoising
Atom-level cross-attention and diffusion denoising are central to AlphaFold 3's generative capabilities, particularly in refining atom positions. This involves a denoising diffusion head that iteratively refines structural predictions, guided by transformer components and noise level embeddings.

The denoising process is orchestrated by the [`DiffusionHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L110) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py). This module acts as the core denoiser, predicting refined atom positions from noisy inputs. It leverages a series of attention mechanisms and feed-forward networks, incorporating contextual information at both token and atom levels. A key aspect of this is the conditioning of the model on various input features and the current noise level through learnable embeddings. This allows the model to adapt its denoising operation based on the current state of structural uncertainty.

Within the [`DiffusionHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L110), atom-level cross-attention mechanisms are crucial for processing atomic details. These are implemented as an encoder ([`atom_cross_att_encoder`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L126)) and a decoder ([`atom_cross_att_decoder`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py#L370)) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/atom_cross_attention.py). The encoder transforms atom-level information into token features, which are then processed by a transformer block. The decoder subsequently translates these refined token features back into specific 3D updates for atom positions. This bidirectional flow ensures that both global (token-level) and local (atom-level) structural contexts are effectively integrated.

The architecture further utilizes transformer components, detailed in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_transformer.py). These include self-attention and cross-attention modules, alongside adaptive normalization and initialization techniques that allow the network to adjust its behavior based on conditioning information. The adaptive mechanisms are particularly important for diffusion models, which often condition on continuous variables like noise level or time. The noise level itself is encoded using Fourier embeddings, generated by [`noise_embeddings`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/noise_level_embeddings.py#L144) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/noise_level_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/noise_level_embeddings.py), which provide a robust way to represent the continuous noise schedule within the neural network.

The [`sample`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L306) function within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py) demonstrates how these components come together for structure generation. It iteratively applies the [`DiffusionHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/diffusion_head.py#L110) to progressively reduce noise, starting from random Gaussian noise and refining the atom positions until a coherent molecular structure is predicted. This iterative refinement, combined with rigid body augmentations, allows the model to explore and converge on plausible structural configurations. The overall pipeline ensures that the model can generate high-quality atomic coordinates by effectively integrating various levels of biological information and leveraging advanced neural network architectures.

### Confidence Scoring and Structural Analysis Utilities
Confidence scoring and structural analysis utilities provide mechanisms to assess the quality of predicted molecular structures and to identify potential issues within them. The [`ConfidenceHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py#L38) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/confidence_head.py) is central to calculating key confidence metrics. It processes the model's internal representations to predict various scores such as Predicted Aligned Error (PAE), predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT), and whether a residue is experimentally resolved. These metrics are often represented as binned probability distributions, from which scalar values are derived to quantify confidence. The [`DistogramHead`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/distogram_head.py#L37) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/distogram_head.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/distogram_head.py) complements this by generating binned distance probabilities between residue pairs, which are then used to calculate contact probabilities.

Beyond individual residue or pair-wise confidence, the system also performs comprehensive structural analyses. The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py) module orchestrates the calculation of various derived confidence metrics. This includes solvent accessible surface area (rASA) to identify disordered regions and a clash detection mechanism that identifies steric overlaps within a predicted structure. The module aggregates these different confidence measures and structural properties to compute an overall ranking score, which helps in evaluating and comparing multiple model predictions. These utilities are crucial for interpreting model outputs and for further post-processing, as detailed in [Macromolecular Data Processing Pipeline](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-macromolecular-data-processing-pipeline) and [Confidence Scoring and Structural Analysis Utilities](#core-model-architecture-and-pipeline-confidence-scoring-and-structural-analysis-utilities). The [`post_process_inference_result`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py#L57) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/post_processing.py) uses these confidence metrics to create standardized output formats, including CIF files and JSON summaries of confidence. This function also handles the inclusion of metadata and versioning information for the predicted structures. Data structures for managing these confidence scores and structural information are defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidence_types.py).

### Haiku Modules and Optimization Utilities
AlphaFold 3 leverages a suite of custom Haiku modules and optimization utilities to enhance numerical stability, manage memory, and improve computational efficiency, particularly in the context of mixed-precision training and large-scale JAX computations.

Core Haiku modules are customized to address the specific demands of molecular modeling. For instance, the [`LayerNorm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py#L50) module ([`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py)) incorporates an [`upcast`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py#L53) option, which temporarily promotes lower-precision inputs (e.g., [`bfloat16`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/model_config.py#L34), [`float16`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/output.md#L25)) to [`float32`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L505) during normalization to prevent numerical instability, then casts them back. Similarly, the [`Linear`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py#L197) module ([`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/haiku_modules.py)) is designed for flexibility, supporting arbitrary input tensor ranks, configurable weight initializers, and an option to transpose weights for memory optimization on accelerators like TPUs. It also includes an optimized path for scalar inputs, bypassing [`jnp.einsum`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/modules.py#L123) for improved efficiency.

Memory management and throughput optimization for large datasets are critical, leading to the development of sharded mapping utilities. The [`sharded_map`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py#L64) and [`sharded_apply`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py#L106) functions ([`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py)) enable the processing of large batches of data by dividing them into smaller, manageable "shards." This approach prevents out-of-memory errors by applying operations to chunks of data sequentially and then reassembling the results. This sharding mechanism is particularly useful for inference with large batches, where the [`inference_subbatch`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/mapping.py#L226) function can split arguments into sub-batches, process each, and concatenate the outputs.

Beyond core modules and sharding, a set of general utilities ([`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/utils.py)) supports data processing. This includes [`remove_invalidly_typed_feats`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/utils.py#L35) for filtering features to ensure compatibility with hardware accelerators, and a [`bfloat16_context`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/utils.py#L55) manager which, in conjunction with [`bfloat16_getter`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/utils.py#L46), ensures that Haiku parameters intended for [`jnp.bfloat16`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L505) are correctly typed during initialization. The [`mask_mean`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/components/utils.py#L60) function provides a robust way to compute the mean of an array while accounting for a mask, handling broadcasting and preventing division by zero, which is essential for various masked computations within the model.

## Geometric Primitives and Operations
The AlphaFold 3 codebase includes a dedicated module for JAX-compatible geometric primitives, operations, and utilities. This module, found under [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax), is designed to handle 3D vectors, rotation matrices, and rigid transformations using a "struct-of-arrays" design. This approach optimizes performance within JAX, facilitating efficient batch operations and seamless integration with JAX's automatic differentiation and compilation capabilities.

Central to this module are the [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) for 3D vectors, [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) for 3D rotation matrices, and [`Rigid3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) for rigid transformations, which combine rotation and translation. These classes support fundamental geometric operations such as vector arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), cross and dot products, and norm calculations. For rotations, functionalities include inversion, application to points, and composition. The [`Rigid3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) further allows for the composition of transformations, inversion, and the application of transformations to points. A key capability is the ability to compute optimal rigid transformations for aligning point sets, which is crucial for structural superposition tasks.

The "struct-of-arrays" design, implemented via the [`StructOfArray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py#L199) decorator from [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py), ensures that these geometric objects are efficient for JAX computations. This design stores components (e.g., x, y, z coordinates of a vector, or individual elements of a rotation matrix) in separate arrays rather than as structures within a single array. This avoids potential performance bottlenecks and precision issues that can arise in high-performance computing environments, especially with mixed-precision operations.

Beyond core transformations, the module provides utilities for calculating distances, such as [`square_euclidean_distance`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L142) and [`euclidean_distance`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L180), and angular measurements like [`dihedral_angle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L200) for torsion angles. It also includes functions for robust weighted means, [`weighted_mean`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/confidences.py#L239) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/utils.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/utils.py), which prevent numerical instability when dealing with zero sums in weights. The [`alphafold3.jax.geometry`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L25) module serves as a unified access point for these functionalities, simplifying their use throughout the AlphaFold 3 codebase.

### Struct-of-Arrays Design for JAX Compatibility
AlphaFold 3 leverages a "Struct-of-Arrays" (SoA) design pattern for its JAX-compatible geometric primitives, which optimizes performance by treating collections of geometric entities as arrays of components rather than arrays of objects. This design is critical for efficient batch operations, array-like indexing, and seamless integration with JAX's automatic differentiation and compilation capabilities.

The [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry) directory defines the core components implementing this pattern. Central to this is the [`StructOfArray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py#L199) decorator, found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py). This decorator transforms standard Python [`dataclasses`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L33) into JAX-compatible structures that behave like "structs of arrays." When applied to a dataclass, it injects array-like behaviors such as slicing ([`__getitem__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L178)), length ([`__len__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/table.py#L128)), and properties for [`shape`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure_tables.py#L190) and [`dtype`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/output.md#L25). Importantly, it registers the decorated dataclass as a JAX pytree node, allowing JAX transformations like [`jax.vmap`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/featurization.py#L47) and [`jax.jit`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L488) to operate smoothly on these structures. It also enforces shape and data type consistency across the internal arrays, ensuring data integrity within the SoA.

Key geometric structures like [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) (3D vectors), [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) (3D rotation matrices), and [`Rigid3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) (rigid transformations combining rotation and translation) are built upon this [`StructOfArray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py#L199) pattern.

*   The [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py), represents 3D vectors by storing their [`x`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L51), [`y`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L52), and [`z`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L53) components as separate JAX arrays. This enables optimized element-wise arithmetic operations and geometric calculations such as dot products, cross products, and norm computations.
*   The [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) class, implemented in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py), manages 3D rotation matrices. It stores the nine components of the matrix as individual JAX arrays, facilitating efficient operations like inversion, application to points, and composition of rotations. It also supports robust construction methods, including those based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) for numerical stability.
*   The [`Rigid3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) class, located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py), encapsulates a 3D rigid transformation by combining a [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) for rotation and a [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) for translation. This class supports operations such as transformation composition, inversion, and the application of transformations to points. A notable feature is its ability to compute the optimal rigid transformation for aligning one set of points to another, which is fundamental for structural alignment tasks.

This consistent application of the SoA design ensures that all these geometric primitives benefit from JAX's performance optimizations, making them suitable for high-throughput computations in machine learning models like AlphaFold 3. The main types and functions from these modules are aggregated and re-exported through [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/__init__.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/__init__.py), providing a unified and convenient interface for their use.

### 3D Vector (`Vec3Array`) Operations
The [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py), provides a JAX-compatible representation for 3D vectors. This class utilizes a struct-of-arrays design, where the x, y, and z components of a collection of vectors are stored in separate JAX arrays. This design choice is aimed at optimizing performance and numerical precision, particularly on accelerator hardware like TPUs, by facilitating vectorized operations. The [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class integrates with JAX's pytree mechanisms through the [`StructOfArray`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/struct_of_array.py#L199) decorator, allowing seamless use with JAX transformations such as [`jax.vmap`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/network/featurization.py#L47) and [`jax.jit`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L488). For more information on this design, see [Struct-of-Arrays Design for JAX Compatibility](#geometric-primitives-and-operations-struct-of-arrays-design-for-jax-compatibility).

The [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class supports fundamental vector arithmetic, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, all of which are overloaded operators for intuitive use. It also provides methods for geometric calculations:
*   [`cross`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L87) and [`dot`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L94): Compute the cross and dot products of vectors.
*   [`norm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L98) and [`norm2`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L106): Calculate the L2 norm (magnitude) and squared L2 norm, respectively. [`norm`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L98) includes numerical stability features to prevent issues with very small values.
*   [`normalized`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L109): Returns a unit vector.

Conversion utilities such as [`to_array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L122) and [`from_array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L126) allow for easy transformation between the [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) object and standard JAX array representations.

Beyond the [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class itself, the module includes related functions that operate on these vector types:
*   [`square_euclidean_distance`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L142) and [`euclidean_distance`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L180): Compute the squared and standard Euclidean distances between two [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) instances.
*   [`dihedral_angle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L200): Calculates the torsion (dihedral) angle between four 3D points represented as vectors, a common operation in molecular geometry.
*   [`random_gaussian_vector`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L229): Generates random vectors with components drawn from a standard normal distribution.

These functionalities are aggregated and re-exported through the top-level [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/__init__.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/__init__.py) module to simplify access.

### 3D Rotation (`Rot3Array`) and Rigid Transformation (`Rigid3Array`) Implementations
The AlphaFold 3 codebase extensively uses [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) for representing 3D rotation matrices and [`Rigid3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) for rigid transformations, both designed for efficient batch operations within a JAX environment. These classes, found primarily in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py), utilize a struct-of-arrays design, where components (e.g., [`xx`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L121), [`xy`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L122) for rotation matrices, or [`x`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L51), [`y`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L52), [`z`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L53) for vectors) are stored as separate arrays rather than interleaved within a single array. This approach optimizes performance on accelerators by aligning with how JAX processes array data. For more information on the struct-of-arrays design, refer to [Struct-of-Arrays Design for JAX Compatibility](#geometric-primitives-and-operations-struct-of-arrays-design-for-jax-compatibility).

The [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) class encapsulates a 3x3 rotation matrix. It supports fundamental matrix operations such as computing its [`inverse`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L133) (which is simply its transpose for rotation matrices) and applying the rotation to a 3D point ([`apply_to_point`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L141)). Multiple [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118) instances can be composed using matrix multiplication ([`__matmul__`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L153)), allowing for sequential transformations. Various methods are provided for constructing rotation matrices, including [`from_two_vectors`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L168) to define a rotation based on two directional vectors, [`from_quaternion`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L209) for conversion from quaternion representation, and [`from_svd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L237) which uses Singular Value Decomposition for robust construction from arbitrary 3x3 matrices, even when they are not perfectly orthonormal.

Building upon [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118), the [`Rigid3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L109) class represents a rigid body transformation, which combines a 3D rotation ([`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118)) with a 3D translation ([`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38)). Like [`Rot3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L118), it supports composition via matrix multiplication and can compute its [`inverse`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L133). It also provides methods to [`apply_to_point`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rotation_matrix.py#L141) or apply the inverse transformation to a point. A key functionality is [`from_point_alignment`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py#L181), which determines the optimal rigid transformation to align one set of points to another. This is achieved by computing a weighted covariance matrix between the two sets of points and then deriving the rotation and translation components. The [`Vec3Array`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L38) class and its operations are detailed in [3D Vector (`Vec3Array`) Operations](#geometric-primitives-and-operations-3d-vector-vec3array-operations).

## Model Scoring and Evaluation
Molecular structures predicted by AlphaFold 3 are scored and evaluated using a suite of tools that perform structural alignment, calculate RMSD, detect and compare chirality, and generate pseudo-beta atom positions. These functions are primarily located within the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring) directory.

Structural alignment and Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) calculations are performed to quantify differences between predicted and ground truth structures. The [`align`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L68) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py) aligns two sets of 3D coordinates by computing a least squares best-fit rotation matrix, which can then be used to calculate per-atom deviations and the overall RMSD between the structures. This is a common method for evaluating the global similarity of molecular models.

For ligand molecules, chirality detection and comparison are critical for assessing the stereochemical correctness of predictions. The [`compare_chirality`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L149) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py) identifies chiral centers within a ligand structure and compares them against reference molecules or entries from the Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD). This process involves converting [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) objects to RDKit [`Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L796) objects and then applying RDKit's stereochemistry functionalities.

Pseudo-beta atom positions are generated as a simplified representation of molecular structures, particularly useful for quality assessment. The [`pseudo_beta_fn`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py#L30) function in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py) computes these positions from full atomic data, supporting both JAX and NumPy backends. This abstraction helps in evaluating model quality without needing to consider every atom, streamlining downstream analysis.

### Structural Alignment and RMSD Calculation
The AlphaFold 3 model repository includes functionalities for structural alignment and calculating Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) between predicted and reference molecular structures. These tools, primarily found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py), are essential for evaluating the accuracy of predicted structures.

The process of structural alignment begins with [`transform_ls`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py#L25), which computes a least-squares best-fit rotation matrix. This matrix optimally superimposes one set of 3D coordinates onto another. It achieves this by using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), a numerical method for factoring matrices, to find the rotation that minimizes the squared differences between corresponding points. The alignment operation, performed by [`align`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/hmmalign.py#L68), then applies this calculated transformation to a target set of coordinates, rigidly moving it into the coordinate space of a reference structure.

After alignment, the [`deviations_from_coords`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py#L105) function quantifies the per-atom differences by calculating the Euclidean distance between the aligned coordinates and the ground truth coordinates. This provides a detailed view of where the predicted structure deviates from the reference. Finally, [`rmsd_from_coords`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/alignment.py#L134) consolidates these per-atom deviations into a single metric, the Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD). RMSD is a widely used measure in structural biology to quantify the average distance between the atoms of superimposed molecules, providing a comprehensive assessment of the structural similarity between a predicted model and its known reference.

### Chirality Detection and Comparison for Ligands
The system includes functionalities for detecting and comparing the chirality of ligand molecules within a structure. This process is handled by the functions within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py), which use [`rd_chem`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L40) for molecular operations, focusing on chiral centers typically involving carbon and sulfur atoms.

The [`compare_chirality`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L149) function serves as the main entry point for this process. It takes a [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) object representing the ligand and, optionally, a mapping of reference molecules. If a reference molecule is not provided for a specific ligand, the system attempts to retrieve molecular information from the Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD) based on the ligand's residue name using [`_maybe_mol_from_ccd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L127). The ligand's structure is then converted into an [`rd_chem.Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L60) object via [`_mol_from_ligand_struc`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L80).

Once [`rd_chem.Mol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/data/tools/rdkit_utils.py#L60) objects are available for both the test ligand and its reference, the [`_chiral_match`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L58) function compares their chirality. This comparison involves identifying chiral centers in both molecules using [`_find_chiral_centres`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/chirality.py#L33) and verifying that all chiral centers in the test molecule match those in the reference. The system accommodates scenarios where the ligand molecule might be a subset of the reference molecule.
