The output is a dictionary indicating whether the chirality of each ligand chain matches its reference.

### Pseudo-Beta Atom Generation
Pseudo-beta atom positions are generated from full atomic data to simplify structural representations for tasks like quality assessment. The function [`pseudo_beta_fn`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py#L30) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py) computes these positions and their corresponding masks. It can operate with either JAX or NumPy backends, determined by the [`use_jax`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/scoring/scoring.py#L35) argument. For each residue, the pseudo-beta atom's index is determined based on its amino acid type, and specific handling is in place for ligands, where their pseudo-beta index is set to 0, typically corresponding to the first dense atom position. This process extracts the relevant coordinates and masks using [`take_along_axis`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/data3.py#L77) for efficient processing.

## Common Utilities and Constants
The AlphaFold 3 codebase includes a foundational set of utilities and constants that underpin its molecular modeling capabilities. This shared infrastructure ensures consistent data handling, configuration management, and access to critical molecular definitions across various modules.

A robust configuration management system, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py), enables the creation of flexible and nested configuration objects. This system automatically converts configuration dictionaries into typed data structures and allows for specifying default factories, which simplifies the process of defining and loading model parameters.

For managing biological input data, the codebase defines specialized structures for various entities like protein, RNA, DNA chains, and ligands in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py). These structures support deserialization from and serialization to different JSON dialects (AlphaFold 3 and AlphaFoldServer) and mmCIF formats, facilitating interoperability with external data sources. The system includes validation mechanisms to ensure data integrity, handles sequence modifications, and processes Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) and structural templates.

Secure data loading is addressed by the [`safe_pickle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L28) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py). This module provides a restricted wrapper around Python's [`pickle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_test.py#L29) functionality, allowing only an explicit allowlist of built-in, innocuous types to be unpickled. This prevents arbitrary code execution from potentially malicious or corrupted pickled data files, crucial for maintaining the integrity of constant data distributed with the repository.

Access to external data files and resources is managed through the [`resources`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L49) module in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/resources.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/resources.py). This module provides utilities to locate files relative to the package root, open them in various modes, and traverse resource directories, ensuring consistent access to necessary external assets.

The definition of molecular properties and constants is centralized in the [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants) directory. This includes a comprehensive mapping of atom types for proteins and nucleic acids, along with structured representations such as [`ATOM37`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L143) and [`ATOM14`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L154) in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py). These definitions are critical for consistent atom identification and data storage in fixed-size arrays.

Chemical component properties, derived from the Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD), are managed by [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py). This includes the [`Ccd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L46) class, which loads CCD data from a pickle file and provides dictionary-like access to component information, with support for user-defined overrides. Additionally, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py) defines predefined sets of chemical components, categorizing ligands and crystallization aids for specialized handling. Tools in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters) are responsible for converting raw CCD CIF files into these efficient pickled formats.

Standardization of residue names and chain types is handled in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/residue_names.py) and [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/mmcif_names.py). These files provide mappings between three-letter and one-letter residue codes, categorize residue types (e.g., standard, unknown, gap), and define utility functions to infer and standardize polymer types from mmCIF data.

A static periodic table of elements, including atomic numbers, symbols, and weights, is defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/periodic_table.py). This provides a consistent and efficient lookup for elemental properties, which is foundational for various molecular operations.

Finally, specific constants related to amino acid side chain torsion angles, such as [`CHI_ANGLES_ATOMS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py#L28) and [`CHI_ANGLES_MASK`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py#L99), are defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/side_chains.py). These constants are essential for calculating and masking chi angles in protein structures, directly supporting the model's ability to predict detailed side chain conformations.

### Input Data Structures for Biological Entities
Biological input data for AlphaFold 3 is managed through a set of structured data classes defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py). These classes represent various molecular entities and their associated information, ultimately encapsulated within a central [`Input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L976) object.

Specific chain types are defined for proteins, RNA, and DNA, along with a distinct type for ligands:
*   [`ProteinChain`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L183): Represents a protein, including its sequence, post-translational modifications, and associated Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) and structural templates.
*   [`RnaChain`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L481): Represents an RNA molecule, incorporating its sequence, modifications, and MSAs.
*   [`DnaChain`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L690): Represents a DNA molecule, similar to [`RnaChain`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L481) but for DNA-specific modifications.
*   [`Ligand`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L834): Represents a ligand, identified either by Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) IDs or by a SMILES string.

Structural template information, used as a reference for predictions, is handled by the [`Template`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L98) class, which stores an mmCIF string and a mapping of query residues to template residues.

The [`Input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L976) dataclass serves as the primary container for a complete biological system. It aggregates various [`chains`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L114) (which can be any combination of protein, RNA, DNA, or ligand), assigns a [`name`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/structure.py#L427), and includes [`rng_seeds`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1001) for model execution randomness. It also stores [`bonded_atom_pairs`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1002) to define inter-chain chemical bonds and can incorporate [`user_ccd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1003) for custom chemical components.

The system supports both serialization and deserialization of these input structures. [`Input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L976) objects can be created from JSON (supporting both AlphaFold 3 and AlphaFoldServer dialects) or mmCIF formats using methods like [`from_json`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1152) and [`from_mmcif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/parsing.py#L408). Conversely, an [`Input`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L976) object can be converted back into JSON via [`to_json`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1485) or transformed into a [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) object for internal model processing via [`to_structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L1414). The conversion to [`structure.Structure`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L88) involves mapping chain sequences and modifications to CCD codes, which are standardized representations of chemical components.

Utility functions are provided for reading compressed external data files (like MSAs or mmCIFs) referenced within JSON inputs, ensuring paths are correctly resolved relative to the input file. The system prioritizes data integrity through extensive validation during object initialization and parsing, checking for consistent IDs, valid sequences, and correct formatting of bond information. Additionally, the design uses immutable data structures, where modifications typically return new instances, enhancing predictability. Default values for missing fields (such as MSAs or templates) can be populated via [`fill_missing_fields`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/folding_input.py#L468). For more information on the underlying configuration system, refer to [Common Utilities and Constants](#common-utilities-and-constants).

### Atom Type and Chemical Component Definitions
AlphaFold 3 manages detailed definitions of common atom types for proteins and nucleic acids, along with structured mappings and fixed-size atom representations to ensure consistent identification and data storage during molecular modeling. This includes the comprehensive handling of Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD) data through a dedicated [`Ccd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L46) class and [`ComponentInfo`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L117) dataclass, which incorporate efficient processing and caching mechanisms.

The system defines various atom type constants in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py), such as [`RESIDUE_ATOMS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L102) (a mapping of residue names to their constituent atoms) and [`PROTEIN_BACKBONE_ATOMS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L127). Specialized fixed-size atom representations like [`ATOM37`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L143) (for 37 common protein atom types) and [`ATOM14`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L154) (a more compact representation) are used to standardize atom data storage, particularly in contexts where all residues need to be padded to a uniform size. Similarly, [`ATOM29`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L253) provides a fixed-size representation for nucleic acid atom types. The system also accounts for protonation states through [`PROTONATION_HYDROGENS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/atom_types.py#L264), which identifies hydrogen atoms whose presence is dependent on a residue's protonation.

For chemical component management, the [`Ccd`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L46) class, defined in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py), serves as the primary interface for accessing Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD) information. It loads CCD data from a pre-processed pickle file and supports user-provided custom CCD entries for overrides or extensions. The [`ComponentInfo`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L117) dataclass provides a structured and type-safe representation of chemical component data, including properties like name, type, formula, and SMILES. Functions like [`mmcif_to_info`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L128) parse raw mmCIF data into [`ComponentInfo`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L117) objects, while [`component_name_to_info`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L183) retrieves [`ComponentInfo`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L117) for a given residue name. Caching mechanisms, such as those applied to [`_load_ccd_pickle_cached`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L38) and [`component_name_to_info`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L183), optimize performance by avoiding redundant data loading and processing. The system also includes utilities, like [`type_symbol`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L190), to determine the element type of a specific atom within a chemical component.

Additionally, [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py) manages predefined sets of chemical components, categorizing ligands and crystallization aids. These sets, such as [`GLYCAN_LINKING_LIGANDS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py#L36) and [`COMMON_CRYSTALLIZATION_AIDS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_component_sets.py#L43), are loaded from a pickled data file, ensuring immutability for data integrity. The generation and processing of these chemical component data sets are handled by scripts within [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters), which convert raw CCD CIF files into pickled Python objects and further categorize them into specific sets, utilizing secure data handling through [`safe_pickle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L28). See [Secure Data Loading with Restricted Pickle](#common-utilities-and-constants-secure-data-loading-with-restricted-pickle) for more details on secure data handling.

### Chemical Component Data Generation and Processing
The Chemical Components Dictionary (CCD) defines the properties of every residue and ligand referred to in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). AlphaFold 3 processes this raw CCD data to convert it into a more usable format for its models, and to categorize specific chemical components into predefined sets. This process involves two main stages: converting raw CCD CIF files into pickled Python objects, and subsequently categorizing these components.

The first stage is handled by the script found in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/ccd_pickle_gen.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/ccd_pickle_gen.py). This script reads a CCD file, which is typically in CIF format and potentially gzipped, and parses its contents using [`cif_dict.parse_multi_data_cif`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/structure/mmcif.py#L124) from the C++ parsing utilities (see [CIF Data Structures and Serialization](#data-parsing-and-preprocessing-cif-data-structures-and-serialization)). The parsed data is then serialized into a Python pickle file. This conversion optimizes access and storage of the extensive CCD information.

Following the initial conversion, the script located in [`/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/chemical_component_sets_gen.py`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/converters/chemical_component_sets_gen.py) further processes the pickled CCD. Its primary function is to identify and categorize chemical components as linking glycans, other glycans, or ions. This categorization is crucial for downstream model operations that might treat these molecular types differently. The script loads the pre-generated CCD pickle file using [`safe_pickle.load`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L43), which ensures secure data handling by allowing only explicitly trusted types during deserialization (see [Secure Data Loading with Restricted Pickle](#common-utilities-and-constants-secure-data-loading-with-restricted-pickle)). It then iterates through each chemical component, applying pattern matching on their type and name fields to classify them. The classified components are stored as immutable [`frozenset`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L54) objects within a dictionary, which is then saved to a new pickle file. These processed sets are later utilized for various model inputs and chemical component definitions (see [Atom Type and Chemical Component Definitions](#common-utilities-and-constants-atom-type-and-chemical-component-definitions)).

### Secure Data Loading with Restricted Pickle
The [`safe_pickle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/constants/chemical_components.py#L28) module provides a secure mechanism for loading trusted, pickled constant data. This module is designed to prevent arbitrary code execution, a common security vulnerability associated with [`pickle`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_test.py#L29) when processing untrusted data. It implements this by strictly limiting the types of objects that can be unpickled.

The core of this security mechanism is the [`_RestrictedUnpickler`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) class, which overrides the standard [`pickle.Unpickler`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51)'s [`find_class`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L54) method. This override ensures that only a predefined allowlist of built-in, innocuous types—such as [`NoneType`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/base_config.py#L37), [`bool`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L444), [`bytes`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold_data_test.py#L71), [`dict`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/parsers/cpp/cif_dict_lib.h#L125), [`float`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/jax/geometry/vector.py#L32), [`frozenset`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/model/features.py#L54), [`int`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L142), [`list`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L75), [`set`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/README.md#L22), [`str`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/docs/input.md#L140), and [`tuple`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/run_alphafold.py#L1076)—can be successfully unpickled. Any attempt to load an object of a type not present in this [`_ALLOWED_BUILTINS`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L36) allowlist results in a [`pickle.UnpicklingError`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L58), thereby preventing the deserialization of potentially malicious objects.

The module offers a straightforward [`load`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L61) function as its main public interface. This function takes a file-like object and uses [`_RestrictedUnpickler`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/src/alphafold3/common/safe_pickle.py#L51) to safely deserialize the pickled data, enforcing the type restrictions. This approach ensures that only data structures and basic types that are inherently safe and cannot execute arbitrary code are processed, protecting the system from security exploits when loading pre-computed or static data distributed with the repository. For other common utilities, see [Common Utilities and Constants](#common-utilities-and-constants).
